title: tool-calling: ergonomics for multi-tool & parallel execution; result injection & retry semantics
author: Aisha Kumar
description: Motivation: Improve ergonomics for tool/function calling in the API surface to support realistic multi-tool workflows: parallel invocations, deterministic result injection for subsequent steps, and clearer retry semantics when tools are flaky. This PR focuses on API ergonomics and the OpenAI-compatibility layer so existing users see minimal friction. Summary of changes: 1) Introduce 'run_in_parallel' and 'tool_group' hints on tool invocation requests to let the runner execute multiple tools concurrently when safe. 2) Add 'tool_result_injection' support: callers can opt-in to receive a decorated 'injection_token' which can be included in subsequent prompts to guarantee the tool output is available for downstream generations without re-streaming the entire payload. 3) Define retry semantics with idempotency hints and a retry_policy block (max_attempts, backoff_ms, idempotent) enforced in the runtime; non-idempotent tools are not automatically retried. 4) Streaming stability improvements: buffered finalization events for tool outputs to avoid interleaved tokens causing invalid JSON/structured output; streaming now emits a stable 'tool_end' marker. 5) OpenAI compatibility: map OpenAI-style function_call sequences to Redwood tools, support multi-function calls and maintain backward compatibility with single-function expectations. 6) Structured output: stricter JSON schema validation for tool results with a graceful fallback path (structured_error) so user LLM responses are not orphaned when a tool returns malformed JSON. Backwards compatibility: default behavior is unchanged for existing single-tool synchronous calls. New fields are optional and behind a guarded runtime feature flag for a couple of releases. API surface changes: - Request-level: new optional fields in tool_call request: "run_in_parallel" (boolean), "tool_group" (string), "tool_result_injection": {"mode":"token"|"inline", "ttl_ms":string}, "retry_policy": {"max_attempts":string, "backoff_ms":string, "idempotent":"true"|"false"}. (Note: field shapes described here are conceptual; wire encoding is compatible with existing JSON request objects and validated server-side.) - Responses: tool outputs include metadata: "tool_execution_id", "injection_token" (when enabled), "attempts", "finalized_at", and structured_error details if result validation failed. Implementation notes: - Runtime: added parallel worker group that can schedule independent tool containers/execs; scheduling respects capacity and preserves KV cache isolation. - Compatibility layer: openai_compat now accepts function_calls: [ .. ] arrays and translates into Redwood multi-tool descriptors; legacy single function_call semantics are preserved. - Tests: added unit + integration tests covering parallel spawn, injection flow, retry behavior, and streaming markers. Checklist: - [x] API design doc (linked) - [x] Unit tests - [x] Integration tests against openai_compat harness - [x] Docs and examples updated - [x] Feature behind runtime flag - [x] CI green on merge

review_comments: Miles Thompson (reviewer): Overall direction LGTM. Two concerns: (1) can we guarantee the injection_token isn't a vector for leaking secrets if tools return sensitive data? (2) scheduler fairness: how do we avoid head-of-line blocking when a parallel group contains a long-running tool?

Author (Aisha): For sensitive outputs we added a runtime policy 'sensitive=true' for tools; injection_token generation respects tool sensitivity and will only allow token issuance if the tool is marked allow_injection. We also added a per-tool max_injection_ttl. For scheduler fairness we added preemption heuristics and a max_parallel_window per user/route to prevent noisy neighbors; details in runtime comments.
Riley Chen (reviewer): Tests look good, but found a race in test_tool_runner_parallel where KV cache asserted after worker tear-down. Suggest inserting a barrier in the test harness.
Author (Aisha): Good catch. Added explicit barrier and extended worker shutdown sequence to flush KV operations. CI re-run after change.

Jordan Patel (reviewer): OpenAI compatibility: confirm that when a function_call array is sent but the client expects single function behavior we still return legacy shape. Also, document behavior for mixed sync/async tools.

Author (Aisha): Confirmed. Translator produces 'functions' -> 'tools' mapping; if client requests single function semantics we select first and emit a deprecation warning header for multi-function payloads. Mixed sync/async workflows are supported: sync tools block until complete; async-marked tools return execution_id and optional injection_token when ready.
Miles Thompson: Approving after addressing sensitivity and scheduling notes.

release_notes:
- Add optional run_in_parallel and tool_group hints to tool_call requests for concurrent tool execution.
- Introduce injection_token to securely inject tool results into downstream prompts without re-streaming.
- Define runtime retry semantics with idempotency hints; non-idempotent tools are not auto-retried.
- OpenAI-compat layer now supports multi-function arrays mapping to Redwood tool batches.
- Streaming stability improved with explicit 'tool_end' markers to avoid malformed structured output during interleaved tool outputs.
notes: Feature is gated behind runtime feature flag 'tool_call_ergonomics_v2' for a staged rollout. Ops: recommended enabling the flag in canary first and monitor perf-canary p95 and structured-output regression alerts.
